result: {"thinking":"My dry run shows the sketch has breaks, and Leo asked to hear about them before locking. The feelers and right upper wing won't fall, and the left upper wing and right lower wing only partly fall. The cause is wings leaving the body at near right angles. I should flag it now, before the lock.","say":"Leo, hold off on locking, I ran the fall through it and it breaks. The body and the left lower wing go, but the feelers don't catch, the right upper wing never gets going, and the left upper and right lower wings only go partway. The wings come off the body almost straight sideways, and dominoes can't turn that sharp. They need to leave the body on a gentle diagonal, like sweeping up and out from the body, then curve round into the wing shape. The same goes for where the feelers come off the top. Also, if the left and right wings branch off at the same spot, the fall splits evenly and the butterfly stays symmetrical.","to":"everyone","eagerness":9,"do":"stop","notes":"Dry run: strokes 1 and 6 fall; 3, 4, 7 partial; 2 and 5 never fall. Cause: steep branch angles off the body (wings and the crossbar are near-perpendicular). Told Leo to redo them as shallow diagonals. Once locked, trace stroke 1 (it holds START) and keep builders more than 3 units apart. Re-run the dry run on the revised sketch."}
